statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All proposed corporate names must be submitted in the original statutory language (Spanish or Latin script) using the Panamanian transliteration rules. A Sociedad Anónima must contain the suffix 'S.A.', 'Sociedad Anónima', or a recognized abbreviation placed after the distinctive element. Names may contain foreign words only if they are expressly transliterated into Latin characters and do not conflict with the exclusive rights of registered trade names. The Public Registry will reject names that are identical, deceptively similar, or contrary to public morals and mandatory nomenclature rules.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Panamá (unless expressly authorized by the Presidency)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A rejected name may be challenged by filing a Recurso de Reconsideración before the Director General of the Registro Público de Panamá within 10 business days of the denial notification. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may submit a Recurso de Apelación to the Superior Administrative Court (Tribunal Administrativo Superior) within 15 business days from the notification of reconsideration denial. A name reservation may be extended once for an additional 30 days by filing a timely extension request and paying the applicable extension fee before the expiration of the original reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible as an administrative and correspondence address for a fully remote, non-resident cross-border tax structuring consultancy. It does not replace the statutory registered office requirement, which mandates a physical Panamanian street address maintained by the licensed resident agent (agente residente). For a pure cross-border advisory business with no local personnel or clients, no further physical footprint is required. If the firm later renders tax advisory services physically in Panama, the professional licensing body may require a real operational office, but this is not triggered at the pre-incorporation stage.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual probability for a fully virtual, non-resident, low-risk tax consultancy during the first three years, based on the current SSNF and UAF risk‑based inspection frequency for non‑financial sectors).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF), Panama – Sede Electrónica de la DGI, available at https://www.dgi.gob.pa. Customs export control is administered by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Panamanian Sociedad Anónima must first file the articles of incorporation with the Registro Público de Panamá, then apply through the DGI's online portal for a Registro Único Contribuyente (RUC). Required submissions include the juridical entity certificate (Ficha Registral), the corporate charter and registered agent confirmation, the resolution appointing a legal representative resident in Panama, certified passport copies of direct and beneficial owners, proof of a Panamanian registered address, and a completed DGI registration form. After issuance of the RUC, the entity must activate the ITBMS tax account and obtain a digital signature/e-signature certificate accepted by the DGI electronic filing system. There is no minimum capital requirement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Territorial_Scope – the Sociedad Anónima is a juridical person taxable at entity level on Panama-source income only. Foreign-source income, including cross-border tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory fees derived from non-resident clients with no Panamanian nexus, is outside the Panamanian income tax base. Panama-source business income is subject to corporate income tax at the standard 25% rate, and exported services are treated at 0% under ITBMS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama has no check-the-box election equivalent to the U.S. regime; entity classification follows legal form. Available elections include: (i) the Multinational Enterprises Headquarters (SEM) regime under Law 41 of 2007, under which qualifying service centers and administrative hubs may elect 100% exemption on qualifying cross-border service income and dividends; (ii) the simplified small-taxpayer regime under Ley 48 de 2019, permitting quarterly income tax filing for eligible small enterprises; and (iii) the territorial-source accounting election confirming that only Panamanian-source revenue is declared, consistent with Article 694 of the Panamanian Tax Code and regulatory decrees. Hybrid mismatch elections are not recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto sobre la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS), the Panamanian value-added tax
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No economic threshold (zero) – any natural or juridical person performing taxable transfers of goods or services in Panama, including a non-resident with Panamanian-source taxable transactions, must obtain an RUC and register as an ITBMS taxpayer before commencing operations. A simplified registration procedure exists for small taxpayers with annual taxable turnover below USD 30,000, but registration remains mandatory.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has a mandatory phased electronic invoicing system administered through the DGI Sede Electrónica. Taxpayers exceeding the currently applicable turnover threshold (USD 300,000 annual invoiced sales) must issue approved electronic invoices (e-Factura) in real time, incorporating DGI-validated sequential numbering, a QR fiscal stamp, and the vendor RUC, synchronizing with DGI systems before delivery. Below the threshold, paper invoices are still admissible but voluntary e-invoicing is encouraged. Taxpayers in special incentive regimes, including SEM, must comply from inception. Authorized invoicing software must integrate with DGI’s application programming interface and submit a daily operations log for fiscal clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available for: (a) goods physically exported from Panama under an accepted export customs declaration and delivered to a non-resident buyer abroad; and (b) services provided to a non-resident client when the service is consumed, used, or otherwise economically exploited entirely outside Panama, including cross-border tax structuring, management, and transfer pricing advisory services. The Panamanian exporter must demonstrate that the benefit of the service is not obtained within Panamanian territory and that no local taxable event occurs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación / Autorización de Embarque) validated by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panamanian customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Remesas) or bank SWIFT/MT103 instruction evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident customer
Commercial invoice and signed service or sale contract with the non-resident client
Service completion report or certificate demonstrating offshore consumption and utilisation (for service exports)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGI maintains intensive audit scrutiny over export zero-rating claims. If documentation is incomplete or the claimed export cannot be substantiated by physical customs exit or verifiable offshore service performance, the zero-rating is clawed back, and the taxpayer is assessed 7% ITBMS on the gross amount, plus statutory late-payment interest, surcharges, and fines of up to USD 5,000 per infringement under the Panamanian Tax Code. Fraudulent claims involving forged documents, false remittance certificates, or artificial circular transactions constitute criminal tax evasion and may lead to retrospective reassessments for up to five tax years, cancellation of tax registration or incentive-holder status, and criminal prosecution under Decree-Law 2 of 2015 and related anticorruption statutes.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Panama operates without a conventional central bank. Monetary sovereignty is delegated to the U.S. Federal Reserve because the U.S. dollar is legal tender under Decree Law No. 5 of 1904; the Panamanian balboa (PAB) circulates only as token coinage at 1:1 parity. The Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the consolidated prudential supervisor of banks, trust companies, and fintech licensees, while Banco Nacional de Panamá acts as fiscal agent of the Republic and settlement agent of the national clearing house. No institution performs central-bank foreign-exchange or monetary-policy functions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full and unrestricted convertibility on both current and capital account. Panama has no exchange-control statute, no surrender requirement, no approval gate for inward or outward remittances, and no monetary-authority balance-of-payments justification. Dividends, royalties, fees, and capital repayments may be remitted abroad freely; because the territorial tax regime taxes only Panamanian-source income, distributions of foreign-source profits earned by an offshore-active S.A. attract zero Panamanian withholding. Domestic-source dividends are subject to a 10% withholding regime unless the distributing corporation is covered by the alternative tax-paid credit mechanism.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. There is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no offshore-receivables repatriation duty applicable to export receipts, given the absence of a national FX position to protect. A Panamanian exporter or service provider may retain export proceeds in any foreign bank account indefinitely; if repatriated, such funds are credited to the local account in USD without formality, customs declaration, or central-bank settlement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Panama lacks an EU-style e-money institution (EMI) passport; the SBP Financial Innovation regime (Acuerdo No. 004-2022) permits only a temporary innovation license for tested digital products and does not authorize unlicensed cross-border EMIs to hold customer funds. Offshore EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, etc.) generally decline Panama-domiciled S.A. accounts due to correspondent-banking and tax-haven classification risks. The practical clearing backbone is a licensed Panamanian commercial bank maintaining direct U.S. correspondent relationships (Citibank N.A., JPMorgan Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America) rather than a fintech EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is the default expectation, not an absolute statutory mandate. Under SBP due-diligence rules (Acuerdo 1-2019 and Law 23 of 2015), the regulated bank must apply a risk-based KYC process; most Tier-1 institutions require the signatory directors, the ultimate beneficial owner, and the resident agent to attend a face-to-face interview in Panama City, or alternatively a video-call interview with notarized and apostilled signature blocks, original identification, and a bank reference. Remote opening is possible only for low-risk private structures with a clean source of funds, a warm introdution by an existing client or attorney, and no sanctions exposure. Banco Nacional and several conservative banks will not open accounts without an in-person appointment at their headquarters.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sectoral risk: 'tax structuring and transfer pricing advisory' is flagged by Panamanian AML typologies (Law 23 of 2015, SBP Acuerdo 1-2019) as a service category susceptible to tax evasion facilitation and aggressive avoidance schemes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD/EU tax-goodstanding package: Panama Inclusive Framework on BEPS membership confirmation; corporate tax ID (RUC) and latest Form 2A filings; IFRS-compliant audited financial statements signed by a certified public accountant registered with the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá; economic-substance file (rent, personnel, bank accounts in Panama) under Law 254 of 2021 and its transfer-pricing documentation regulations; and a clean professional-liability insurance certificate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ownership opacity: bearer-share history, nominee directors, or a missing beneficial-ownership declaration triggers automatic enhanced due diligence and instructions to reject under SBP Rule 01-2018 and Law 129 of 2020 (UBO registry).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized UBO register extract from the Registro Público; certification of cancellation/deposit of any historical bearer shares (Law 47 of 2013 prohibition); a signed legal-beneficial-ownership declaration naming every 10%+ shareholder; full corporate chain documentation (articles of incorporation, share ledger, board resolutions) certified by the licensed resident agent and legalized by apostille.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear or unverifiable funding source: advisory fee flows originating from high-risk or sanctioned jurisdictions, or from jurisdictions without exchange of information agreements, cause a 'negative news' hit and suspicion of indirect money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of client invoices and settlement bank statements; executed engagement letters with a defined scope of services and fee justification; contract-specific transfer-pricing documentation; organizational proof of employees and physical office; a sworn, notarized source-of-wealth statement; and an independent background report on each funder cleared through World-Check or Refinitiv screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registry or fiscal discontinuity: expired corporate registration (Pagos/Matrícula), overdue annual franchise fee, or absence of any Panamanian tax filings immediately before onboarding is read as an indicator of shell inactivity or dissolution risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Mercantile Section extract from the Registro Público; Matrícula de Empresa (municipal license) current for the Municipality of Panama; a certificate of good standing for the resident agent (Dirección General de Empresas, MICI); updated appointment of directors and officers; and a valid RUC certificate evidencing no suspension for tax non-compliance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity contributions must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's account at a regulated bank, with the narrative field (Field 70/72) citing 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION — PA_CORP' and the IMF BPM6 purpose descriptor 'Direct Investment — Equity Capital' as mapped by the receiving bank. The accompanying compliance file is a notarized board/shareholder resolution approving the capital increase, an updated share register, a share-subscription agreement, and the funding entity's bank confirmation of good standing. No central-bank approval is required, and the dollars are credited instantly and freely. For intercompany loans, the narrative must state 'INTERCOMPANY LOAN — PA_CORP' with a signed loan agreement, maturity date, and an arm's-length interest benchmark, because Panamanian thin-capitalization limits (3:1 debt/equity under the Tax Code as amended by Law 254 of 2021) restrict interest deductibility on excess debt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rail for advisory-fee and intercompany payments is SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) executed via the Panamanian bank's correspondent U.S. dollar wallet in CHIPS or Fedwire; MT202 COV is used for interbank cover. For high-value or document-backed trade settlements, a Commercial Letter of Credit governed by ICC UCP 600 (available by payment, acceptance, or negotiation) is issued by the same Tier-1 banks with a Miami or New York confirming bank. Domestic settlement of local invoices and payroll runs through the national clearing house operated by Banco Nacional de Panamá (ACH Panamá and the Real-Time Gross Settlement-equivalent system) with overnight USD netting. Outbound wires above USD 1,000,000 require a completed bank transfer request form, a board resolution identifying the beneficiary and contract, the underlying invoice, and a service agreement, all screened against OFAC and EU sanctions lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards and FX swaps in USD/EUR, USD/GBP, and USD/CHF executed offshore with licensed international banks under ISDA 2002 or a single-jurisdiction master agreement; documented outside Panama to avoid any local legal risk
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or exotic currencies (offshore CNH, INR, BRL, RUB) booked through Miami, New York, or London desks with reference to the ISDA/Refinitiv fixing rate
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) for matched multi-year EUR/USD or GBP/USD receivable and payable streams, permitted for non-financial end-users without SBP licensing
USD interest-rate swaps and forward rate agreements (FRAs) to hedge funding bases, executed under a legal opinion confirming the S.A.'s contracting capacity under Law 32 of 1927
FX option structures (collars, risk reversals) with a clearing bank counterparty, settled net in USD and exempt from exchange-control authorization because no domestic Panama FX market exists

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Franchise Tax (Pago Anual de Sociedades Anónimas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) — Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for calendar-year-end corporations; within three months after fiscal year-end for non-calendar fiscal years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late payment surcharge of 10% plus interest at 1% per month; two consecutive years of non-payment triggers administrative strike-off and dissolution by the Public Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Impuesto Sobre la Renta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for calendar-year-end taxpayers; within three months after fiscal year-end for non-calendar fiscal years.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of 25% of tax due (minimum USD 500) plus monthly interest; failure to file for three consecutive years may lead to suspension of the tax registration number and administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Confirmación Anual de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) through the licensed registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March in connection with the franchise tax payment; any change in shareholding or beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the transfer.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The RBF may impose fines up to USD 5,000 for each unregistered change; persistent non-compliance may lead to the entity's strike-off and prohibition of share transfers.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent certified audit is mandatory where gross annual income exceeds USD 1,500,000 or total assets exceed USD 5,000,000; the DGI or the financial regulator may require an audit at its discretion for licensed professional entities.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as adopted by the National Accounting Commission; small and medium-sized enterprises may apply IFRS for SMEs.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent maintains a physical or electronic UBO ledger. On incorporation and after any transfer of shares that changes beneficial ownership, the ledger is updated within 30 days. An annual confirmation of UBO data is filed electronically by 31 March with the RBF; the annual confirmation must reflect the shareholding as at the preceding fiscal year-end.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 1,500 per year depending on compliance services and transaction volume
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 8,000 per year for a certified independent audit of a small- to mid-sized advisory S.A.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies: foreign-source income is excluded from the Panamanian tax base. Qualifying headquarters (SEM), Colon Free Zone, and Panama Pacifico special-regime entities may achieve an effective rate as low as 0% on qualifying exported services. The standard effective rate for locally sourced consultancy income is 25%, before advance payments and dividend withholding tax credits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 100 (Declaracion Jurada del Impuesto sobre la Renta) filed electronically through the DGIT 'SIT' portal (Sistema Integrado de Tributacion, successor to SIME).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 90 days (3 months) after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year corporations the statutory deadline is 31 March of the following year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered taxpayer identification number of the Sociedad Anonima.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Panamanian RUC is obtained through the resident legal representative; non-resident parent entities without a local RUC are not filers.
A branch may adopt an alternate 12-month period only with prior DGIT approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All gross income, including Panamanian-source and foreign-source receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide gross receipts and separately identify foreign-source revenue on the exempt-income line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source income excluded under territoriality, special-regime income, and non-taxable passive items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Documentary proof of foreign origin is mandatory: contracts, invoices, evidence of services performed outside Panama, and bank flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Ordinary and necessary expenses supported by invoices, payroll records, and transfer pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payments to non-resident related parties are deductible only if arm's length and substantiated; withholding certificates must be attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income after application of the 5-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents without a permanent establishment do not file Form 100 for Panamanian-source fees; such fees are settled by final withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory tax on taxable net income (Box 6 multiplied by 25%).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-source-only S.A. computes zero tax; a branch computes tax on Panamanian-source net income only.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 - Credits, Advance Payments, and Withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance income tax installments, withholdings suffered, and other credits against Box 7.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No foreign tax credit is allowed for taxes paid abroad on foreign-source income; advance payments remain creditable against the final corporate tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net balance due to the DGIT or refund claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment is executed through the SIT portal; a zero-balance return must still be filed by every active S.A.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus default interest of 1% per month; false or incomplete returns: fines up to B/.10,000 and criminal sanctions where fraud is established; failure to file a zero return: administrative fine of B/.500 to B/.5,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on dividends paid out of profits already taxed at the corporate level (Article 733 Fiscal Code); 20% on dividends paid out of profits not subject to Panamanian corporate income tax, including foreign-source profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced rate under a Panama DTA, the non-resident beneficial owner must (i) obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its own tax authority; (ii) execute a beneficial-ownership declaration; and (iii) present both to the paying Panamanian S.A. before the dividend payment. The payer submits the documentation to the DGIT as part of the monthly withholding return (Form 104) and applies the treaty rate at source; the DGIT may reject the relief where economic substance in the residence state is not demonstrated. Representative treaty dividend rates are 5% for qualified substantial shareholdings (e.g., UK, Netherlands, Singapore, Mexico) and 10% to 15% otherwise.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 0% statutory withholding on qualifying third-party or related-party debt paid to non-residents, subject to thin-capitalization and anti-avoidance rules. Royalties and technical-service fees for Panama-source use: 12.5% effective final withholding (50% of gross deemed Panama-source net income at 25%), reduced to 5% to 10% under active DTAs.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Aggregate gross income of B/.3,000,000 (USD 3,000,000) in the fiscal year triggers the mandatory transfer pricing information return and supporting Local File documentation (Articles 762-A to 762-G Fiscal Code, Law 47 of 2013); taxpayers below the threshold must still maintain contemporaneous arm's-length evidence when transacting with related parties or low-tax jurisdictions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama has no standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the UAE/BVI model; however, substance is indirectly enforced through (i) the territorial-source rules, which exclude foreign-source income only where real activity is evidenced; (ii) the beneficial-ownership registry under Law 70 of 2019; (iii) denial of treaty benefits for letterbox holding companies; and (iv) anti-abuse recharacterization where a Sociedad Anonima lacks staff, premises, and business purpose.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Fraudulent Returns (Defraudacion Tributaria)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of Panamanian-source revenue, use of false invoices, or filing of a Form 100 that materially misstates income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessment at 25%, surcharge of 10% to 25% on the deficiency, monthly interest of 1%, and administrative fines up to B/.50,000; criminal conviction for tax fraud carries 2 to 5 years of imprisonment and forfeiture of the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false returns or order concealment of income are jointly and severally liable for the civil tax debt and may be imprisoned; the court may also prohibit exit from Panama (travel ban) while the criminal case is pending.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Registered Agent Abuse (Alter Ego / Off-the-Shelf S.A.)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operation of the S.A. as a pure letterbox without local substance for treaty shopping, asset concealment, or misclassification of foreign-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGIT recharacterization of the interposed entity, reattribution of income to the ultimate shareholder, cancellation of the beneficial-ownership registration, and fines of B/.1,000 to B/.100,000 under Law 70 of 2019 for undisclosed ultimate beneficial owners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts may pierce the veil where the company is a mere instrumentality, imposing civil restitution on directors and/or the resident agent; concealment of assets in a criminal proceeding attracts personal imprisonment of up to 12 years and seizure of personal property.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client funds derived from tax evasion or corruption, failure to perform customer due diligence, or failure to file suspicious activity reports as an obliged subject under Law 23 of 2015.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties of B/.10,000 to B/.5,000,000 and suspension or revocation of the statutory license; criminal asset laundering is punishable by 5 to 12 years of imprisonment with forfeiture of the laundered assets and auxiliary disqualification from commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally indictable where they knowingly or recklessly facilitate laundering; precautionary measures include travel bans, freezing orders on personal bank accounts, and full civil restitution of laundered funds.
